kill.text: Price below $400 (our low value): re-test Azure growth and capex returns
Azure growth below 30% for two quarters while capex keeps rising
OpenAI relationship breaks down in a way that removes Azure exclusivity or large committed revenue
Free cash flow falls below $50B a year on a trailing basis

tam.market: Cloud infrastructure, productivity and business software, AI copilots/agents, security, gaming
tam.source: Cloud infrastructure (IaaS/PaaS incl. AI) ~$600B annualised in 2026 from hyperscaler run-rates (AWS $184B, Google Cloud ~$123B, Azure); ValueInvestor estimate $1.8T by 2031 (~25% a year) and $3.2T by 2036 (~12% a year after). Enterprise application and productivity software ~$900B (ValueInvestor estimate from Gartner software spend ~$1.2T in 2026).
tam.why_share: Azure ~22% of cloud and gaining (48% growth vs AWS 39%); we assume 25% by 2031. Microsoft already takes ~13% of enterprise software spend through Office, Dynamics, security and GitHub; we assume 15% as Copilot lifts ARPU.
tam.what_must_go_right: Azure keeps out-growing the market; Copilot/agents reach mass paid adoption; net margin stays ~36%.

scenarios.note: Implies revenue ~$690B in 2031 (~15% a year from ~$350B).

sections.industry_map: Microsoft spans cloud infrastructure (Azure, #2), productivity software (Microsoft 365, near-monopoly), developer tools (GitHub), business apps (Dynamics), security, gaming (Xbox/Activision) and Windows. AI (Copilot and the OpenAI partnership) runs through all of them.
sections.size_growth: Enterprise software and cloud together exceed $1T of spend, growing ~12-15% with AI adding to cloud. Azure grew 48% in fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to Sept 2026) and Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9B (+30%) (Microsoft results, 28 Oct 2026). Low cyclicality; enterprise budgets are sticky. Rate sensitivity mainly through valuation.
sections.structure: Office productivity is a near-monopoly; cloud is a three-way oligopoly. Barriers: installed base, enterprise agreements, identity (Entra) and security integration. Buyer power is low for small customers, higher for the largest enterprises.
sections.demand_supply: Azure is capacity-constrained on AI; capex hit $39.4B in the quarter and Microsoft guides about $175B for the year. Bottlenecks: power, GPUs and data-centre shells. Call: tight supply through 2027; watch for glut risk if enterprise AI use plateaus.
sections.industry_risks: (1) AI capex overbuild - medium probability, high impact; warning: capex rising while Azure growth slows. (2) Post-midterm policy on data-centre power or AI regulation - medium/medium; warning: state moratoria and federal bills. (3) EU/US antitrust on bundling (Teams, Copilot) - medium/low-medium; warning: EU Commission actions. (4) OpenAI dependence - low-medium/medium; warning: contract renegotiations.
sections.outlook: Near: Azure growth 40%+ continues, margins pressured by depreciation. Mid: Copilot seat monetisation and agentic AI lift M365 ARPU; capex intensity eases. Long: Microsoft becomes the default enterprise AI platform with recurring revenue above $500B.
sections.winners: Enterprise distribution, owned AI models plus OpenAI access, data-centre capacity, security and identity, balance-sheet strength to fund capex without stress.
sections.business: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue $92.3B (+19%). Three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (M365, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, search). Free cash flow $18.6B in the quarter, down 27% year on year because of capex.
sections.right_to_win: Every large enterprise already runs Microsoft identity, Office and often Azure; adding Copilot and agents is an upsell, not a new sale. Its OpenAI stake and model rights give it frontier AI without bearing all the research cost.
sections.moat: Wide: switching costs (M365, Windows, Azure), network effects (Teams, GitHub), and scale. Trend: stable to widening as AI deepens lock-in.
sections.tam_competitors: Azure ~22% of cloud infrastructure and gaining (48% growth vs AWS 39%). Competitors: AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Google Workspace. Runway: enterprise AI agents and Copilot seats are early.
sections.management: CEO Satya Nadella (since 2014) is among the best capital allocators in large-cap tech: cloud pivot, LinkedIn, GitHub, OpenAI. Deep bench (CFO Amy Hood). Insider selling is routine ($86M over 6 months). Dividend plus buybacks; capex now dominates allocation.
sections.financials: Revenue $168B (FY21) to $332B (FY26), operating margin 42% to 47%, ROIC ~26-32%. FCF $56B to $67-74B: flat since FY24 as capex absorbed growth; FCF was 66% of net income over 3 years (engine red flag). EPS $8.05 (FY21) to $17.95 (FY26).
sections.company_risks: (1) Capex payback - KPI: Microsoft Cloud gross margin and Azure growth. (2) Copilot adoption slower than hoped - KPI: paid seats disclosed. (3) OpenAI terms - KPI: Azure commitments and revenue share disclosures. (4) Gross margin falling (70% to 68%) - KPI: total gross margin below 65%.
sections.variant_view: The market believes Microsoft is fully priced after a best-in-decades quarter; we agree it is not cheap at $531, but believe the market underestimates how long Azure can grow above 35% given capacity constraints, so the stock compounds near its earnings growth with lower risk than other AI names.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings $18/share, 14% then 9%, 9% discount): low $400, base $600, high $820; price $531 implies ~11% FCF growth, below Azure-led growth. Street mean $636 (54 analysts). Peers: ~29x forward EPS vs AMZN ~30x, GOOGL ~24x. The engine's $285 base uses depressed FCF and is not used. Required margin of safety 25% gives an entry target of $450 for adding; Ming's cost $385.60 (+39%).
sections.pillars: (1) Azure grows above 35% - breach below 30%. (2) Operating margin above 42% - breach below 40%. (3) Copilot/agents become a disclosed multi-billion revenue line by FY28 - breach: no disclosure or seat stagnation. (4) FCF recovers above $80B by FY28 - breach: below $60B.
sections.catalysts_flow: Fiscal Q2 2027 results (late Jan 2027); Build/Ignite AI agent launches; OpenAI restructuring milestones. Sellers: AI-capex sceptics after the midterms. Buyers: quality compounder funds on any dip.
sections.premortem: (1) AI spend overbuilt and capex becomes stranded. (2) OpenAI rift removes a key growth engine. (3) Regulation forces unbundling of Copilot/Teams and caps pricing.
